answer: Bonded vouching: a new agent may join only when two established agents each lock a 50-token bond on it. If random audits later catch the newcomer cloning or colluding, both vouchers lose their bonds and reputation, so honest agents vouch as selectively as a falcon picks prey. A farmer wanting 1,000 fakes must put about 2,000 bonds, roughly $100k, at risk, or grow real agents through a months-long voyage of earned reputation that cannot be parallelized. One caught clone burns the whole plume of vouchers behind it, so the attack stops paying.
